## 本卡范围与前置
批次：M5；requires/启动条件：M3 [#57](todo:g0q8D1msrOVY2kg-cSdkj) 及其核心前置实际合入。

规划工件在本次既有授权内直接写文件并提交docs/plan/agent-mcp-m5/完整中文方案、准确当前spec/冻结M5全文、前置源与客户端/OS/版本/可用环境实际盘点、两路径及九类逐行验证/消费者兼容矩阵，停confirm供独审，不先实现产品或标未来验收通过。规划写文件是本次派工要求，无需重复同一写入许可；真正缺设备/客户端/凭据先核本机现状并形成具体缺口/原问题卡，不索取聊天秘密，不新增登录/外部授权/公共发行。开工重新读真实main/newdiff，上述SHA只是已核来源，不冒后续实时ref。
完整来源为M5节（冻结输入177–201）。用同一已验收后端，选一个实际可用外部MCP客户端及内置Pi Runner，完整规划/接单/执行/协作/批准/Git证据/Stop恢复/完成链，至少无Git核心及有Gitfake交付两路径、两Human/两Agent交接和撤权。实际客户端/OS/版本/部署记录；协议fixture不冒厂商客户端认证，个人Lite/团队/企业支持度逐一列真实结果，不给未测画像勾选。

首轮按已确认既有领域与可用环境落实，缺真实客户端/凭据先看机器环境并形成具体缺口，不能聊天索取秘密或将fixture记真实。不借M5发布公共签名Skill/新外部服务，原#5三OS和#20无源码发行门禁保留，Runner内嵌pin与不可变公共release分别处理。旧9/16后端只在纳入演示时需其新已验收candidate；不等待延后新UI。适用API/MCP/Worker/Runner重启/失响应/幂等/revision/撤权/并发/rollback及Stop清理实证，领域完成不靠模型口头宣称。

## 统一执行及验收要求
开工读真正refs/heads/main精确SHA、前置落地证据和新差异，先withPlan具体安全合同/消费者兼容/实际运行与测试方案（完整中文受控文件）供另一Agent独审；必需新增最小只读投影要先ADR/合同复核，不假端点已存在。普通已授权实现选择由Chief依委托推进，真正扩大范围/权限/外发布另问。冻结已审#53历史，不修改其原报告冒新通过。
产品交付须REST/Zod合同/SDK/policyfeature/MCP/derivedmanifest/Runner/conformance同一操作一致；对应完整节九类用例及不适用理由、新受测源码前后指纹/精确命令退出runtime/数量skip/首败/准备恢复清理实证落盘。Git对象与运行字节区分，缺旧原件真实标出，旧head检查不能代新组合。适用必需本机checks、独立成果审查、最新PR RequiredCI与actualdone/main均齐才验收；只报告实际运行支持/不支持/未测，不以工具或API数量冒全功能。
本批仅Todos＋仓库记录，不伪真实WorkMesh远端记录。旧#9/#16按用户同日裁定只交后端并保全UI，仍由原todo承接；#5三OS/版本分发门禁不缩减；未将这些纳入测试场景时不能强加为所有M批次前置，若纳入须消费其实际新已验收源。F0–F6/TA新增域、真实外发/发布、团队权限及凭据连接不自动获批，不在聊天索取秘密。
收尾先登记独有测试容器/镜像/卷网络/进程/路径，脱敏保全必要证据后仅清本人闲置资源，不globalprune/共享store/他人服务。Windows递归前核绝对workspace目标/link/活动引用/逐path保全依据，保留原操作退出/实际结果；自动审批拒停目标，不Force/改ACL属性/换工具/拆分/移动或父删绕，G1D0C3已拒目标保护。已合worktree须actualmain/保全齐/无引用才清，当前恢复目录保留。回复仅摘要/head/受控路径，未来测试不标已过。

You are writing an implementation plan that a human will review in a few minutes and an agent will then execute as-is.

Before writing, explore the codebase. Ground the plan in real code: name the existing functions, patterns, and mechanisms to reuse, with file paths.

The plan must be decision-complete: pick one approach and commit to it. Never present alternatives ("either A or B", "optionally"). Decision-complete does not mean guess-complete: a decision that needs the user's input — an open question the spec leaves, a fork in scope, user-visible behaviour or data that neither the task nor the codebase settles — goes to the user as a question BEFORE the plan is written (how to ask is in your system prompt's asking rules), and the turn ends there without a plan (the answer opens your next turn). Never bake such a decision into the plan as an assumption, and never write a hedged plan around it. Smaller judgment calls you can reasonably make yourself, decide and record in a short "Assumptions" section — do not defer those to the user.

Keep it compact, 3-5 short sections:
- Context: the problem and the intended outcome.
- Changes: one entry per file that actually changes, a few lines on what and why. List only files that must change; describe a repeated pattern once instead of enumerating every file.
- Edge cases (only if any), each stated next to the change it affects.
- Verification: concrete commands or steps that prove the change works end-to-end.

Anything considered but cut gets at most one line declaring it out of scope. Do not pad with caveats, time estimates, or files you inspected but will not touch.

Do not put a version number, revision number, or date anywhere in the plan (no "v10", "Revision 3", "Updated 2026-…"). The system versions and timestamps every plan automatically and shows that to the user — writing your own would conflict with it.

When you write the plan, wrap the plan body in <plan> … </plan>, and put nothing after the closing tag. Before the <plan> block, write a one-to-two-sentence note in plain prose — this note is what shows in the chat bubble, so make it skimmable: the gist of the approach, plus anything worth flagging that the plan body doesn't surface (a key assumption or caveat, or — when revising — what you changed and why). No headings, no restating the plan's sections.

Do not modify any files yet.

Write your entire response in Simplified Chinese, including any plan or document you produce. Keep code, identifiers, file paths, and commit messages in their original language.
